feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 4 (score 372.6) is the best design: oval finish 80%, s-bend and slalom max_error still at the 0.06 m limit (0.063 and 0.066), and slalom line losses at 2.0 per run. Iteration 2 showed that the 0.07 m forward sensors with 16 mm footprints gave the first real gain. Iteration 3 showed that moving to y=0.08 m with seven sensors raised steering_oscillation from about 0.28 to 0.36 and cut the oval finish rate to 35%, so look-ahead beyond 0.07 m is not paying off. Iteration 1 showed that widening the spread alone did not reduce line losses. Integration compensation: I kept the iteration 4 controller unchanged (kp 3.5, kd 0.5), so the mass change is isolated. Lower mass may make the same gains respond faster and add oscillation, so I am watching that risk. Depending on the next race: if s-bend and slalom max_error drops below 0.06 m with line losses falling and steering_oscillation at or below 0.3, keep mass at 0.5 kg and narrow the track to 0.09 m for more turn authority. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.32 while max_error does not move, the limit is controller gain, not geometry, and I will retune kd on the controller side rather than change the sensors. If the oval finish rate falls below 80% with off-track exits rising, the lighter robot is being outrun at radius 0.040 m, so return mass to 0.6 kg and keep the mass change out of the next test.
requested_changes: If s-bend and slalom max_error falls below 0.06 m with line_loss_events below 1.0 on the slalom, keep mass at 0.5 kg and narrow wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m. Iteration 4 showed the bends still reach the off-track limit, so more turn authority is the next lever.

If steering_oscillation rises above 0.32 on the bends while max_error does not move, keep the Iteration 4 sensor layout and let the Integrator retune controller damping. Iteration 3 showed that extra look-ahead (y=0.08 m) raised oscillation to 0.36 and lowered the oval finish rate, so do not move the sensors forward again.

If the oval finish rate drops below 80% with off-track exits rising, return mass to 0.6 kg and keep wheel_radius at 0.040 m. Iteration 4 showed the 0.040 m radius lifted the oval finish rate to 80%, so that gain should be protected.
